expected_level_description: You can: - work to support wider organisational objectives beyond your immediate goals​ - track emerging internal and external issues over time that could affect the work of teams across the organisation - take action to solve or mitigate problems by influencing colleagues across the organisation

You can: - communicate with technical and non-technical stakeholders at all levels, and across organisations, using architecture communication techniques​ - mediate between people in difficult architectural discussions - gain support from business and technical stakeholders for architectural initiatives with high levels of risk, impact and complexity - coach and support others in architecture communication
You can: - identify appropriate contractual frameworks and approaches - identify, evaluate and select appropriate suppliers

You can: - work collaboratively in a group, actively networking with others - adapt feedback to ensure it’s effective and lasting - use your initiative to identify problems or issues in the team dynamic and rectify them - identify issues through Agile ‘health checks’ with the team, and help to stimulate the right responses

You can: - make and guide architectural design decisions characterised by medium risk and complexity - identify and address architectural risks that affect multiple teams or domains - use architectural governance and assurance to make design decisions and manage technical risks at the appropriate level - contribute to the development of architectural governance and assurance

You can: - lead the framing of a problem characterised by high complexity, complication, or risk so that a solution can be created - coach others in defining problems and describing appropriate options for solutions - help others challenge requirements and assumptions, and identify opportunities when defining problems and solution options

You can: - define strategies or visions across teams that align with organisational objectives - direct the implementation of a strategy or vision, for example, by creating roadmaps or plans - define architectural principles and patterns - develop or maintain strategy in response to feedback and findings

skill: Technical design throughout the life cycle
expected_level_description: You can: - create technical designs characterised by high risk, impact, and complexity - lead and guide others in creating technical designs that achieve organisational objectives - use feedback to optimise and refine standards for technical designs throughout the life cycle

You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload
You can: - set interoperability standards and strategy for the organisation - lead national or cross-organisation standards work - assure the design of critical integrations across many systems

You can: - lead data protection impact assessments and information sharing agreements - advise teams on lawful basis, consent, confidentiality, and retention - investigate incidents and recommend improvements

You can: - lead hazard identification and risk assessment for a product or change - write and maintain hazard logs and clinical safety case reports - agree risk controls with product teams and check that they work - advise teams on applying clinical risk management standards
You can: - follow a software life cycle process that meets medical device standards - produce the records that such a process requires
You can: - record and update risks for your area - suggest controls and track actions
You can: - line manage a team, setting objectives and running appraisals - support wellbeing and manage attendance, performance, and conduct - plan the team's development and succession
